articles.title: 7 cool indie games from GDC 2025
articles.summary: GDC 2025 featured some intriguing indie games like Dreams of Another, Faraway, and Herdling.
articles.body: The Game Developers Conference, an annual gathering that brings thousands of game developers to San Francisco, has just wrapped up. While most of the event is about networking and interesting talks about game design and technology, there were also a bunch of unreleased indie games that we got to check out. Yes, much of video games in 2025 will probably be defined by the Nintendo Switch 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI. But based on the games we played, there might be some really fun smaller titles that could be huge hits this year, too. Here are a few of our favorites that we’re looking forward to. Dreams of Another [Media: Dreams of Another is a shooter, but you use your gun to create the world around you instead of destroying it. The game’s graphics have a dreamy, deconstructed quality to them, and when you shoot things, the colorful, unfocused scenes you see will solidify into things like buildings and people. Unexpectedly, my brief demo ended with a more traditional shootout against a sentient manhole cover. (I even lobbed a couple grenades to try and destroy it.) But I’m intrigued by the overall concept, and I look forward to seeing what developer Q-Games does with it in the final version of the game.—JP Faraway [Media: In Faraway, you play as a shooting star and try to make constellations. The game requires just pressing and holding one button to spin around other stars, create a trail, and essentially play a celestial game of connect the dots. It’s a simple concept, but I was impressed by it immediately. In just a 10-minute demo, I was really starting to get the hang of using my shooting star’s momentum to perfectly swing around a star to make elaborate and high-scoring constellations. That’s all the time it took to make Faraway far and away my favorite game of the show.—JP Haste: Broken Worlds [Media: Haste: Broken Worlds is kind of like a 3D version of the classic mobile game Tiny Wings. You play as Zoe, a girl who runs forward at blinding speed through procedurally generated levels. Like with Tiny Wings, there are rolling hills you can launch from for added height, and if you time your fall right into the curve of another hill, you’ll get a satisfying “perfect” message and a boost to a meter that lets you pull out a hoverboard. The game has a roguelike structure, so you’ll get to pick and choose different types of levels to tackle as you make your way through a run. On the show floor, I was awful, dying within the first few levels before I had to hand the controller to the next person in line. But as soon as I got back to my hotel room, I downloaded the game’s free demo on Steam.—JP Herdling [Media: Herdling tasks you with herding mysterious, fluffy beasts. In my demo, the character starts in a dark city before quickly coming upon three adorable beasts that reminded me of a big goat mixed with Sesame Street’s Mr. Snuffleupagus. Your goal is to get them out of the city and out to wilder pastures. You coax the animals forward from behind with a magic stick, and while they generally follow your directions, they are sometimes difficult to direct. More than once, my herd of three walked right into a wall. By the end of the demo, however, I really started to care for my fluffy friends, especially since you can name them — though I can only imagine the cruel ways the developers will pull on my heartstrings over the course of the full adventure.—JP Hotel Barcelona [Media: This is sort of the video game equivalent of a supergroup. Goichi “Suda51” Suda (best known for off-kilter games like Killer 7 and No More Heroes) has teamed up with Hidetaka “Swery65” Suehiro (the writer and director behind Deadly Premonition and, more recently, The Good Life) on an extremely challenging and roguelike game set in a world inspired by slasher movies. In the short time I had with the game, I died multiple times, but the twitchy action felt very satisfying, especially once I got the hang of the controls. There’s a neat feature where you can fight alongside a ghost image of your previous run, which seems like it will come in handy. What I didn’t get to experience was the inevitable surreal twist the two creators have put on the horror setting, but the core is solid.—AW My Arms Are Longer Now [Media: Slapstick comedy games are really coming into their own of late. And if you loved Untitled Goose Game or Thank Goodness You’re Here, this is definitely one to keep an eye on. The name really says it all: you control an unseemly long and stretchy arm and attempt to... do things, most of which are illegal. The level I played took place on a moving train, and you were tasked with stealing items from passengers while remaining undetected (probably because of how terrifying the arm is). There’s a puzzle element to it; at one point, I needed to take a briefcase from a sleeping businessman, only to find it was chained to his wrist. It’s absurd, of course, but that’s exactly the appeal.—AW To a T [Media: To a T is a delightful game about a teenager permanently stuck in a T pose. The game is from Katamari series creator Keita Takahashi, so, of course, it’s wacky and silly. My demo featured an elaborate tooth-brushing sequence, musical numbers, and a talking giraffe. But the demo also hinted at the character’s fear of school and bullying over their T-pose condition. I was surprised how much that made me care for the character, and if the story sticks the landing, it could make a game that might have been pure silliness something more thoughtful. It’s out on May 28th.—JP

articles.title: How to Navigate Pierce Brown's Red Rising Sci-Fi Series
articles.summary: New to Red Rising? Here's what you need to know.
articles.body:
In the future, the human race has been divided into 14 different color castes that determine every individual's role and placement in the hierarchical structure of society. This underlying idea is at the core of Pierce Brown’s epic science fiction series, Red Rising , and tells the story of one man, Darrow of Lykos, and his mission to tear it all down.

First released in 2014, the first title, Red Rising, introduces us to the series' protagonist, Darrow, a Red Helldiver of Mars and the lowest of the citizens. Events out of Darrow’s control put him on a path that will see him go from the bottom of society to the top, becoming a symbol and legend that strikes fear into his enemies and inspires hope in his allies. Unlike many other science fiction series, Red Rising isn’t a tale of a utopian society that has spread out amongst the stars. Instead, it is a world of war, betrayal, and uneasy alliances, where some of the worst societal practices have flourished and evolved. Yet it is still a universe where hope still finds a way to survive, and joy and love can still be found, even in the darkest and most profound places.

Compared to other series, like Brandon Sanderson’s Cosmere or George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire , reading through the Red Rising series is a straightforward affair. The series is divided into two arcs, with the first three novels - Red Rising, Golden Son, and Morning Star- being referred to as the “Red Rising Trilogy”. The second half, which takes place 10 years later, being the “Iron Gold Quadrilogy” and consisting of the remaining novels. Despite being a science fiction series, this series deals with mature themes and graphic violence, and isn’t advised for younger readers.

How Many Books are There in the Red Rising Saga?

Pierce Brown’s Red Rising series will comprise seven books in total, but currently, all but the final book have been released. The first three titles, composing the Red Rising Trilogy, are told strictly through the viewpoint of the character, Darrow. In contrast, the rest of the books, the Iron Gold Quadrilogy, are told through multiple characters' viewpoints.

The first book in the Red Rising Saga, titled “Red Rising”, tells the story of Darrow of Lykos - a Red Helldiver, born in the mines of Mars whose only prospects are to live out his days in the mines, with the belief that he is helping to bring about the terraforming of the planet. A tragic event sets Darrow’s life on an entirely new trajectory, where he now fights as a member of the rebel group Sons of Ares in a bid to overthrow the society that has oppressed him his entire life and bring about equality for mankind. But, to do so, he will have to become what he hates the most.

Picking up two years after the conclusion of Red Rising, Golden Son follows Darrow’s continued exploits as he carefully navigates the Gold society. As his reputation continues to grow, he has to be more careful and not risk being exposed as a Red. Golden Son ratchets up the stakes for Darrow, with some fantastic twists and tense white-knuckle moments that will leave readers biting at the bit to dive right into the third book after finishing this one. Where Brown’s first novel felt like a mix of Hunger Games and Ender’s Game, Golden Sun starts to define what the series will be moving forward, and how it sets itself apart from other science fiction series.

Taking place one year after Golden Son, Morning Star sees the Reaper at his lowest yet as he deals with the effects of being betrayed, and his year-long isolation. His work isn’t done yet, however, and his mission must go on, but at what cost? This third book brings the conclusion of the original trilogy of the Red Rising Saga, setting Darrow and his friends on a path they could never have imagined, one that will require relying on old enemies to make it through alive.

Picking up 10 years after Morning Star, the Reaper’s legend continues to grow and has even outgrown the man, as mankind is struggling to adapt to the events of the previous book. Iron Gold marks a departure from the previous books, and a shift for the series, as no longer do they follow strictly Darrow’s perspective and instead show events from the four different views, including Darrow and two brand-new characters, Ephraim ti Horn and Lyria of Lagalos.

The points of view that this follows include Darrow, Lysander, and two new characters, a Red named Lyria and a Gray named Ephraim.

War has come to Mercury. Picking up directly after the events of Iron Gold, Dark Age lives up to its name, being the darkest in tone and subject matter of the series. It’s a book that's overall pretty gruesome and may be difficult for some readers to get through. The repercussions of many of the Reaper’s past decisions and debts have come to be paid. As author Pierce Brown puts it - “The Solar System is at War. No one is safe”.

The points of view in this fifth entry of the Red Rising series include Darrow, Ephraim, Virginia, Lyria, and Lysander.

It has been eight months since the events of Dark Age, and the surviving members of the Republic struggle and prepare for the war that is just over the horizon. After the events of Mercury, the struggle between the Republic and Society has shifted to Mars and beyond, as both sides struggle to secure the needed allies and resources to grasp victory once and for all. Enemies will become unwilling allies, allies who will betray one another, and new threats will arise from the shadows that could throw everything into chaos, but hope can always be found, even in the darkest of nights.

Lightbringer is told through the points of view of four characters (omitting who to avoid potential spoilers)

Red God is currently planned to be the final novel in the Red Rising series, and also the longest. In a brief interview, Brown teased that he hopes that this final book will be released late next year, but only if he is happy with it.

Pierce Brown’s Red Rising: Sons of Ares Omnibus

Taking place before the events of the first book, the Sons of Ares comic series offers a deeper look into the rebel faction and its various actors, who play such an important role in the first few books of the Saga. These comics do contain some massive spoilers for events that are revealed throughout the first three books, and it’s advised that you only read them after completing the third book, Morning Star.

Red Rising: The Board Game, published by the talented team over at Stonemeier Games (the developers of games including Wingspan and Scythe), is a competitive hand management game where players will be playing out cards representing characters from the various books and colors of the Society. This game is not only a good time for fans of the books, but also features some wonderful art that helps give readers a better mental image of this world and its characters, such as Eo, Victra, Sevro, and of course, Darrow.

To avoid spoilers, it’s best to try out this game after you’ve gotten through at least the Iron Age. You can check out my full review of this game for more information on the rules and gameplay.

The final book in the Red Rising series, titled Red God, is currently on the horizon. Although we don't have a specific date as to when the book will be released, we do have an estimation from the author himself . In an interview back in January 2025, Pierce Brown stated that Red God would "most likely" be coming out in Summer 2026.

Pierce Brown has discussed a potential TV adaptaion for quite some time now. In an inteview with Maudes Book Club back in April 2025 , Brown said "it's in development with a streamer," but couldn't say which one. Unfortunately, Brown recently provided an update that the TV series has been abandoned. In the same interview , however, Brown suggested there may be another live action adaptation on the horizon.

In the world of Red Rising, humanity is divided into distinct castes, each associated with a specific color, with individuals born with both a sigil and eye color that correspond to their class. Ruled over by golds, this “Society” has been in charge for over 700 years by the start of the first book. Here is a breakdown of all 14 colors and their respective roles within the Society.

articles.title: Dev Behind Russian Roulette Drinking Game Cancels Steam Demo Plans Following AI Copycat Concerns
articles.summary: The developer behind Russian roulette anime game Drunken Goddess Reflux has canceled its plans for a public Steam demo, citing concerns over potential AI copycats.
articles.body:
The developer behind Russian roulette anime game Drunken Goddess Reflux has canceled its plans for a public Steam demo, citing concerns over potential AI copycats.

Alliance Arts and Who You's path to launch has seemingly been mostly bump-free since it was announced back in April. Featuring ghostly pinks and purples and a gameplay premise described as "shot glass Russian roulette with a demon who loves you enough to kill you," the recent reveal that it would launch this December only made its future feel clearer.

Part of that release date announcement included the promise that a demo would launch October 19, but as explained in an update post on Steam , those plans have changed. What was originally intended to be a public release for the Drunken Goddess Reflux demo has now been canceled in favor of a "closed play session for a limited number of participants." It's a last-minute move Alliance Arts apologized for, but its concerns related to rapidly advancing AI technology were simply too great to ignore.

Drunken Goddess Reflux - Steam Screenshots

"We are concerned that, based on the content of the demo, works imitating or replicating this game's presentation and gameplay could be quickly produced using AI or other tools and released ahead of the game's launch," the developers said in their list of concerns.

In other words, sending a demo out into the wild could open the door for nefarious individuals to use AI to generate a low-effort clone or copycat experience. For a team hoping for a successful launch in just a few months, someone coming in to steal its thunder could potentially throw a wrench into things.

Alliance Arts' fears emerge amid a time when AI is seeping into the gaming industry in ways most may not have ever expected. For example, mods – including mashups of Elden Ring and Super Mario 64 or Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 and Skate – have regularly gone viral on social media in recent weeks. With the controversial technology expanding in new, unforeseen ways every day, it's a risk the Drunken Goddess Reflux weren't willing to take.

Another bullet point concern listed in its message detailed restrictions on posting and streaming gameplay videos, but as the team explained, they "are not currently in a position to properly handle and manage those restrictions." With limited resources to keep nearly unrestricted access to a demo in check, Alliance Arts is moving forward with that closed demo.

"We will therefore hold online play sessions in a closed environment," the developer added, "open to those who have reviewed and agreed in advance to the participation requirements and the rules on posting and streaming gameplay videos."

Players interested in trying the demonic drinking game out were encouraged to join the Discord server presented in the Steam post. Otherwise, Drunken Goddess Reflux is still scheduled to launch on PC via Steam December 8, 2026.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Angel Reese, Natalie Nakase Disagree on Dream Star's Scoreless WNBA Finals 2nd Half
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese and Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase had different reasons for Reese's second-half struggles in Game 1 of the WNBA...
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese produced a fantastic first half in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries . She had 14 points on an efficient 5-for-8 shooting from the field and looked like the best player on the court.

This did not continue in the second half. Reese didn't score a point in the final two quarters, going 0-for-3 from the field and committing three turnovers. Atlanta lost their lead down the stretch and ultimately lost the game 68-64, giving Golden State a 1-0 lead in the finals series.

Reese spoke with the media after the game and was asked what the Valkyries did to limit her shot attempts in the second half.

"I don't think they really did anything. Maybe that was just on me. I wasn't aggressive enough with the ball, and trying to get the ball, and get to my spots. So definitely gonna do a better job of that next game," Reese said.

Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase didn't agree with Reese's take. She was asked about the adjustments her team made against Reese in the second half and praised Valkyries forward Laeticia Amihere, who guarded Reese for much of that half.

"I thought [Amihere] did a fantastic job with that matchup [on Angel]. LA had great energy; again, she was kind of our insight with this game plan, and so you could tell there was a lot of confidence in her matchup," Nakase said.

"[Amihere] was really key tonight for our success," she added, per the WNBA's YouTube channel .

Angel Reese Contact Raised Eyebrows During WNBA Finals

The bottom line is that the Valkyries won Game 1. However, there were some questionable plays involving Reese that could have become a bigger story of the Dream took this WNBA Finals game.

Reese, who received some criticism for what Sophie Cunningham called "dangerous" plays in the WNBA Semifinals, seemed to hit Gabby Williams in the face while the two were going after a ball in the second half. Reese was called for a common foul, but some fans thought the play warranted a closer look to see whether it was a flagrant.

Reese also hit Valkyries star Veronica Burton on the head while Burton went for a layup in the second half. No foul was called on this play, which could have loomed large because Reese was one foul away from fouling out.

But none of this matters now, as the Valkyries are surely just glad they escaped Game 1 with a huge win.

articles.title: WNBA Finals between Valkyries and Dream won’t be pretty, but they’ll be far from boring
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — The problem with two elite defensive teams meeting in the WNBA Finals is that you get two elite defensive teams meeting in the finals. A day...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The problem with two elite defensive teams meeting in the WNBA Finals is that you get two elite defensive teams meeting in the finals. A day like Saturday begins with so much anticipation, particularly around here, where sidewalk tailgates near the arena were being set up by 9:30 a.m. Before tipoff, the outgoing commissioner rightly praised the state of the league, noting the record number of people who paid to see games in person this year.

The competitors, in a happy coincidence, represented franchises at the vanguard of that growth in many ways. This was the setup, as per usual at this time of year. A showcase unveiled. A championship-round pedestal. And then the teams smashed each other's faces into bricks for two hours.

Expecting anything else would mean expecting the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream to operate wildly out of character, and teams do not play for titles by doing that. So the 68-64 win for the Valkyries in Game 1 will not be the exception. It will be the black-and-blue rule. Easy to enjoy for some. Not easy on the eyes for anyone.

The league as a whole might be better served by putting something more aesthetic out there for this final series, especially after a season of record-breaking offense and the thoroughly watchable basketball it created.

And, well, insert shrug emoji. We'll instead get Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase fielding a question about a tangle that led to some sort of leg pain for star forward Gabby Williams on Saturday, and it turns into a real puzzler.

"Which one?" Nakase said, looking up and flipping through her mental game film. "There were a lot of collisions."

Attrition is what the WNBA has to offer over the next couple weeks. Among the numbers that outgoing commissioner Cathy Engelbert cited Saturday to tout this series? Six of the 10 members of the league's all-defensive teams would be on the floor. It is absolutely a skill, and it is absolutely worth appreciating. It's a mastery of the ultimate controllable. As Williams, a first-team all-defense honoree, noted the day before the finals began: A lot of it is just willingness.

Both of these teams are willing. Relentlessly willing. Occasionally overly willing. It can't be said that either side got bullied when players from both teams hit the floor writhing at the same time, whether it was Veronica Burton and Rhyne Howard tumbling to the deck after vying for a rebound or Allisha Gray lying on her back in the paint while Tiffany Hayes lay on her stomach near midcourt.

It's very possible, in fact, that the sequence during which Williams tweaked her leg happened on a free throw. Williams stood at the line. She held her follow-through. Atlanta guard Jordin Canada slid into position to box out the shooter, as basketball players have been taught since time immemorial. And then, after the make, they basically fell over each other.

That was this game, and that is these teams. A car crash even at a full stop.

"It was a long game," Williams said, declaring herself to be OK afterward. "It was a long, physical game."

At least there will be intrigue. Game 1 was taut. It was suffocating. In two seasons, the fans here have created an atmosphere the WNBA would love to replicate in every arena across the league. "Nothing's ever personal," is how Golden State center Kiah Stokes described the vibe of the crowd known as "Ballhalla." Then, on Saturday, after Angel Reese contacted Burton's head on a drive without drawing a whistle, all of Ballhalla booed and notified the game officials that they sucked.

The Dream asked some very interesting questions with their collective effort, actually, after being asked how they'd handle an oppressively loud, hostile environment to start this series. Foremost among them: What if they wanted that?

What if a team with Reese as the spear tip — the sort of player who gets isolated on Valkyries guard Cecilia Zandalasini and then claps in Zandalasini's face as all her dribbling goes nowhere — wants all the smoke, because the smoke is their oxygen?

It didn't work out on Saturday … but then again, it almost did. How hard they take their next turn in Game 2 will be fascinating.

"We're going to look at everything and try to get better, but I mean, we were right there," Dream coach Karl Smesko said. "Right there. So that's why it hurts a little bit. But it also motivates us. We know what we're capable of doing."

The resolution of this finals matchup won't be pretty, which is a little unfortunate given the product that dominated the regular season. But neither will it be boring. They don't call it a scrap because everyone comes out unscathed.

Following the game, Nakase duly checked in on Hayes, who went to the locker room after the play that left her face down on the floor in the final minutes. The coach gave the 14-year veteran a hug, and then a little something extra to the ribs.

"Tough shooting night," Nakase told Hayes, who missed 11 of her 12 attempts from the field.

"It's only going to get better," Hayes replied.

Debatable, given who these teams are in their marrow.

The winners on Saturday are a group that talks about playing with a mentality of heart and hustle, as their coach put it before the game, which conspicuously omits beauty from the equation. No, these WNBA Finals might not be won. They might be survived.

articles.title: WNBA Finals winners and losers include Valkyries' Gabby Williams, Dream's meltdown
articles.summary: The Valkyries took a 1-0 lead in the WNBA Finals over the Dream. Here are winners and losers from Game 1.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Golden State Valkyries are 1-0 in WNBA Finals games after defeating the Atlanta Dream , 68-64 , in the first game in the best-of-seven series on Saturday, Oct 13, at the Chase Center.

The Dream, on the other hand, are 0-10 in the Finals. They are playing in their fourth championship series in franchise history and this one is off to a familiar start.

Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 26 points. Eight other players scored in Golden State's balanced effort. The Valkyries shot 33% and their bench outscored the Dream's 20-6.

The Dream had three players in double figures led by Allisha Gray with 19 points. Angel Reese had a double-double with 14 points and 12 rebounds. Atlanta shot 32% from the field and scored eight points in the fourth quarter.

Here are the winners and losers from Game 1 of the WNBA Finals:

2026 WNBA Finals photos: Atlanta Dream vs. Golden State Valkyries

It took Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams a while to get going, but once she heated up, she never cooled down.

Williams was held scoreless in the first quarter, shooting 0-of-4 from the field and 0-of-3 from the 3-point line. But she came out aggressive in the second quarter and scored 16 of her 26 points in the frame, becoming only the sixth player in WNBA Finals history to record 15 or more points in a quarter.

"Once we all started having fun and the excitement got out, we started to kind of find our way," Williams said. "We always know we're going to find a way somehow. There was a lid on that basket tonight, but that's why we rely on our defense."

It wasn't the most efficient outing for Williams, who shot 8-of-22 from the field, 3-of-11 from the 3-point line and 7-of-8 from the free-throw line, but she was the only Golden State player to finish in double digits. Williams rounded out her stat line with four rebounds, two assists and one steal.

Gabby Williams is headed to the WNBA Finals. See her career in photos

Allisha Gray has been waiting nearly 14 days to play a basketball game. The wait was well worth it. Gray might have lost her shoes at one point ― and even her defender momentarily as she got back up to speed ― but it didn't seem to matter as she scored 19 points and grabbed six rebounds against a gritty Golden State Valkyries defense. She used her used her speed to get downhill, weave through traffic and misdirect. Gray was also good at drawing fouls against Golden State, something the Dream did well during the regular season.

"I felt well. I mean I felt playing out there. Finger felt good ... was able to get through the physicality. Definitely disappointed in the loss, but ... we're gone have a film session. Clean up some of the mistakes we had and be prepared and ready to win Game 2," Gray said postgame.

Laeticia Amihere hadn't played Game 1 of the first round of the WNBA playoffs, a 104-80 win against the Dallas Wings on Sept. 27.

But staying ready for when your number is called has been the way of the Valkyries. And when Amihere's card was pulled in Game 1 the WNBA Finals, she delivered. It wasn't a splashy performance, but Amihere's presence played a huge role in the Valkyries' win.

Amihere played for Atlanta for two seasons in 2023 and 2024. So when Golden State matched up with the Dream, Amihere provided some intel.

"LA did a fantastic job with that matchup. LA had great energy," Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase said. "Again she was kind of our insight with this game plan. You can tell there was a lot of confidence in her matchup, but again of course she's gonna say it's team defense.

"LA just did a phenomenal job and then protecting the rim. She was really key tonight for our success."

Amihere did a little of everything with five points, five rebounds, a steal and a block in 14 minutes. She went 2-for-2, finishing under the rim and immediately provided a needed spark for the Valkyries.

Kaila Charles didn't have the best shooting performance, but she did everything else. Charles pulled down 10 rebounds, including three offensive rebounds. She added a couple of assists, steals and a block to her stat line. She was an overall +13 in the plus/minus box.

Kai (Kaila Charles) made game winning plays tonight," Valkyries guard Gabby Williams said. "Kai made a huge defensive stop into transition, got a wide open layup and those are the kinds of things that ... when our shots aren't falling those are the kind of plays that are gonna win these kinds of games."

Kiah Stokes had the best defensive rating of any center in the WNBA this season, and it's easy to see why when you consider her holistic impact on Golden State's suffocating style.

In Game 1 against Atlanta, Stokes blocked a game-high four shots and grabbed seven rebounds to go with nine points. She secured a crucial defensive rebound and drew the fifth foul on Dream star Angel Reese after Naz Hillmon missed a potential go-ahead 3-pointer with 25 seconds remaining in the game.

Stokes leads the WNBA in rebounds (64) and blocks (16) this postseason.

In addition to her value on the defensive end, Valkyries leading scorer Gabby Williams gave a shoutout to Stokes postgame for setting screens that create space for the Valkyries' best shooters and making possession-saving plays.

"She's probably like the best screener in the league, which isn't really talked about enough," Williams said. "Kiah and (Kaila Charles) made game-winning plays tonight. Kiah got a big (offensive rebound) after I missed a layup. She went up, got the O-board, got the lid off the basket.

"Those are the kinds of things that when our shots aren't falling, those are the kind of plays that are going to win these kinds of games."

The Atlanta Dream had a five-point lead over the Golden State Valkyries heading into the fourth quarter. They were 10 minutes away from stealing Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on the road at Ballhalla.

But then the Dream came undone offensively.

Atlanta was held to eight points in the fourth quarter. The team shot 2-of-20 from the field and 0-of-7 from the 3-point line in the fourth quarter.

"Obviously a tough finish for us," Karl Smesko said after the loss. "Unfortunately, we had kind of one bad defensive quarter where we had a few breakdowns and then one bad offensive quarter in the fourth where we kind of turned it over and didn't have the kind of shot quality that we wanted."

The Dream had a number of self-inflicted wounds in Game 1. Despite entering the WNBA Finals with a playoff-high 24.4 points scored off turnovers, it was the Valkyries who got the best of their opponents. Atlanta conceded 17 points on 12 turnovers, compared to 10 turnovers (eight points conceded) for the Valkyries.

On Saturday, Golden State's depth showed up huge. Four different players scored for the Valkyries as it wracked up 20 points to the Dream's six. DeWanna Bonner, who had been leading Atlanta's bench unit during the postseason, played 13 minutes and scored two points. Isobel Borlase scored the rest of the Dream's bench points. The rest of the bench did not see minutes.

"They're probably the deepest team in the league, and they use their bench quite a bit," Dream head coach Karl Smesko said. "We're gonna have to find our opportunities to get some players some rest (because) we know how physical the Valkyries are and how aggresive they are. How can we buy a minute here, a minute there so that we can be fresh down the stretch?

Dream guard Rhyne Howard's shooting performance

Rhyne Howard did not have the performance needed for the Dream to escape with a victory. Howard scored 12 points in their loss to Golden State, shooting 21.4% from the field (3-for-14). She struggled in the game as the stingy Valkyrie defense forced her into three turnovers on the night.

Howard knows her play was uncharacteristic and hopes to have a better outing in Game 2 on Monday, Oct. 19.

"They forced us into a version of the game of basketball that we don't play," Howard said. "We didn't punch back. We just kind of played to how they were making us play. We're going to have to watch some film and go back and make some adjustments."

Rhyne Howard's basketball journey from Kentucky star to WNBA Finals

Atlanta was the second-best overall rebounding team in the WNBA this regular season (35.6 rpg) and led the league in offensive rebounds per game (10.6). But the Dream faltered on the boards down the stretch in Game 1, missing their last six field goal attempts of the game and letting the Valkyries secure the rebound each time.

Overall, Golden State outrebounded Atlanta, 41-35. A large part of that was due to the Valkyries' bench, which had a 22-3 rebounding advantage over the Dream's bench.

articles.title: Guardians' Parker Messick, Rays' Drew Rasmussen to start Game 5 of ALCS
articles.summary: With the American League Championship Series tied 2-2, the Guardians and Rays are each turning to an All-Star starting pitcher.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — With the American League Championship Series tied 2-2, Game 5 between the Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays will pit All-Star starting pitchers against each other on Sunday, Oct. 18, at Progressive Field.

The Guardians will start rookie Parker Messick, and the Rays will start Drew Rasmussen, their respective managers said after Tampa Bay prevailed 7-3 in Game 4 on Saturday, Oct. 17, in Cleveland .

Guardians-Rays, ALCS Game 1's best photos

Messick is 0-2 in three starts this postseason with a 3.09 ERA and 14 strikeouts in 11⅔ innings. In the regular season, he went 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA and 193 strikeouts in 186⅓ innings. He started Game 2 of the ALCS, a 3-1 Rays win. He allowed three runs (zero earned), six hits and two walks and struck out three in five innings.

Rasmussen is 1-0 in two starts this postseason with a 1.29 ERA and 17 strikeouts in 14 innings. In the regular season, he went 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA with 174 strikeouts in 172 innings. He started Game 1 of the ALCS, a 7-3 Guardians victory. He allowed two runs, eight hits and no walks and struck out seven in six innings.

articles.title: Valkyries survive shooting slump with their usual grit for WNBA Finals win
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — Ballhalla rose in unison, prepared to explode. Just under six minutes remained when the ball found Cecilia Zandalasini in the left corner. Th...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — Ballhalla rose in unison, prepared to explode. Just under six minutes remained when the ball found Cecilia Zandalasini in the left corner.

The previous three minutes had been a rough stretch offensively for Zandalasini. She missed two free throws after getting fouled on a 3-pointer. She followed that by missing a 13-foot turnaround from the left side of the paint, then a missed 26-footer from the right wing.

But this shot? Zandalasini was more open than a highway at midnight. This shot promised redemption. With Golden State down 3, this shot carried the potential for momentum that swings the flow of a game and, thus, these WNBA Finals. It threatened to detonate the fervor in Chase Center until it crumbled on top of the Atlanta Dream.

And Zandalasini, coach Natalie Nakase's favorite floor spacer, whose shooting form is worthy of a gilded frame, took a rhythm dribble and set her feet.

Then airmailed it. Not even close. Another shot swallowed by the Valkyries' offensive abyss.

It was one of those nights for the Valkyries. Tiffany Hayes went 1 of 12 before leaving with injury. Gabby Williams needed 22 shots to score 26 points. Zandalasini, Veronica Burton and Kayla Thornton — three starters who at various points deliver offensive punch — combined to shoot 5 of 19 while scoring 16 points below their collective average this postseason.

"Obviously," Burton said, "we missed a lot of shots. Missed a lot of bunnies. Missed open 3s. I think, initially, we were kind of settling for a lot of 3s."

But the Valkyries have been here before. Brick City. Where the shots won't fall, the dribbling increases, and the offense gets stagnant. They've visited too many times, actually. They know the potholes and alleys. They know the side streets and which street lights are the longest.

Nothing about this air felt rare despite this being a novel stage. They survived Game 1 with a 68-64 win because this stress was far more familiar than foreign.

On every new plateau they reach, their resolve proves greater. They're three wins from being champions. They survived another scare at home. All because they've long given up on the idea of shooting their way out of slumps. They'd rather fight their way out.

"It kind of just fits into who we are," Nakase said. "That's been our identity. We rely on it. We know it's effort. We know it's the details. … It's kind of been our philosophy, especially down the stretch and close games. And you could see that it's just kind of, 'Here we go again.' So it's the same thing. There's a lot of familiarity and composure down the stretch."

The Atlanta defense made sure Golden State would have one of these games. The Dream pressured the ball on the perimeter, disrupting the Valkyries' motion offense. Atlanta's defenders fought around screens and rode drives to force tough finishes. They closed out hard on shooters and threw their weight around when crashing the glass.

Atlanta used its athleticism, wingspan and defensive savvy to muck up the Valkyries' offense. It stymied the Golden State offense. Add in the nerves of the Valkyries' WNBA Finals debut and the ball seemed heavier, the passes shakier. The rim shrank like an Ozempic waist, and points for the team in purple became scarce.

The Valkyries scored 28 points in the second quarter. They scored 26 points in the second half.

"We had the game right where we wanted it," Williams said, "because it just came down to getting stops. That's been our bread and butter all season. So we harp on it so much because we've built great defensive habits for these moments."

As they have so many times before this season, they found themselves trailing and out of rhythm. The stage of the WNBA Finals added to the urgency, for sure, but this still was light compared with being down 16 in a do-or-die Game 3 against Dallas.

They don't panic because they know this feeling. They've spent an entire season getting comfortable with it, fighting to keep their calm when the angst starts to rise with each brick. For Golden State, a struggling offense is a reminder its true calling card is defense and its most championship-worthy trait is resilience.

So when the Valkyries' offense goes astray, their confidence doesn't.

"At the end of the day," Burton said, "we were supercomfortable with where we were, even down 3 with a few minutes left. And I think that is what we've become. Like, no lead makes us nervous. No lead makes this feel uncomfortable. Again, we don't want to get to that position, but we felt in a very good place."

That good place: down 64-61 with fewer than three minutes remaining. That's when Burton blocked a floater by Dream guard Allisha Gray. On the ensuing inbounds, Kaila Charles secured the stop by rebounding Jordin Canada's missed 3.

With points becoming scarce, and the clock dwindling, the Valkyries know where to go for offense. They put the ball in Williams' hands and clear out.

Atlanta's defense, though, is formidable, led by Rhyne Howard on the perimeter and Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese in the back. After a series of screens didn't work, Williams drove on Howard and drew a foul.

Williams made both free throws. This would be how they win this night. At the free throw line.

No pretty shot. No moment to immortalize. Just 2 points earned from the grind.

Perhaps the biggest 2 came courtesy of a Reese foul, grabbing Williams in transition. The two makes by Williams put Golden State ahead 65-64 with 1:18 remaining. Another foul from Reese led to another Valkyries point as she crashed into Kiah Stokes during a rebound.

Williams put the game on ice with a pair of free throws with 4.1 seconds remaining.

"I told you," Valkyries owner Joe Lacob said with a wide grin after the game. "She's the best player in the world."

Golden State closed on a 7-0 run without making a shot.

The Valkyries shot just 4 of 16 in the fourth quarter. But all of the baskets they made were products of the muscle they've developed when their offense wavers.

It was Charles getting a breakaway layup after stealing the rock from Howard. It was a tip-in by Stokes, crashing the glass after a Williams drive. It was a block by Hayes and an outlet pass that led to a Williams fast-break layup.

This was the 21st time this season the Valkyries scored fewer than 80 points. They've won 15 of those games.

"You've got to find different ways to win," Burton said. "And it's just something that we learned. We've won from our defense. We will continue to win from our defense. And that's the beauty about it being our identity is because a lot of times you can't control what happens. Yeah, we would love to clean some things up offensively and hopefully have a better performance on that side of the basketball. But to be able to still win this game when we obviously (still) can have our best outing on that side is big for us."

The Valkyries have plenty to fix before Monday's Game 2. Their shooting, certainly. Their execution. The possessions that often end in desperation heaves. But what they won't have to fix is their relationship with adversity.

They can handle the potholes of Brick City. They're comfortable on its bumpy roads. They're built to win in these streets.

articles.title: Quentin Tarantino Says He's 'Written a Script' for 10th and Final Film, But He Wants to 'Live' Before Making It
articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino has confirmed he's "written a script" for his 10th and final film, but he's going to "live" a little before making it.
articles.body:
Quentin Tarantino has confirmed he's "written a script" for his 10th and final film, but he's going to "live" a little before making it.

The Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood and Kill Bill filmmaker teased his plans for his long-in-development finale movie during an appearance on The Graham Norton Show . He said he has a script for a film he "could" do, and it's one he also happens to "really, really like," but he's got a checklist of things to take care of before diving into it.

"I've written a script that I could do that I really, really like, but I have to do the play and see who I am, right?" Tarantino said, referencing his upcoming West End play, The Popinjay Cavalier.

"I'll finish the play, and then I'll go back, be with my family for a while, and then live and then see what that guy wants to do."

The director's words were in response to a question from show host Graham Norton, who asked about his "10th" and "final film." Tarantino didn't skip a beat when conjuring up his reply, suggesting that, yes, the plan is still for his next film to be his last whenever it does eventually hit screens.

For reference, The Popinjay Cavalier is set to start previews February 23, 2027, and then open one month later, March 18. That means we've got some waiting to do before Tarantino will begin the "then live" phase of his pre-movie plan. How long it will be before he then decides on a script, begins production, and settles on a release date remains to be seen, but don't expect to hear any significant updates for a while.

Tarantino mentioned wanting to finish his career as a movie director at film number 10 a few years before the release of his eighth film, The Hateful Eight , in 2014. As Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood came and went as his ninth project in 2019, his decision to put a cap on his big-screen presence has only become more controversial amongst fans.

A filmmaker with a very specific number of trend-setters – including Pulp Fiction , Inglourious Basterds , and Django Unchained – the idea of intentionally ending his time as an artist has been deemed confusing and disappointing. That doesn't seem to have phased Tarantino one bit, and the time it's taken for him to get started on the final project suggests he's not in any rush to get started.

Rumors surrounding his enigmatic 10th once had moviegoers expecting him to direct what Simon Pegg called a "bats**t crazy" Star Trek film before the director eventually debunked those alleged plans himself . He was also once said to be making a project called The Movie Critic before it, too, was scrapped .

It will be some time before Tarantino directs another movie for theaters, but that doesn't mean an opportunity to see his work on the big screen is too far away. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , a Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood follow-up written by Tarantino and directed by David Fincher , will premiere next month .

articles.title: Antrim SFC: St Brigid's secure historic first Antrim football title
articles.summary: St Brigid's make history in an all-Belfast Antrim SFC final, securing their first senior football title with a 0-21 to 1-16 win over O'Donovan Rossa.
articles.body:
St Brigid's made history in an all-Belfast Antrim SFC final, securing their first senior football title with a 0-21 to 1-16 win over O'Donovan Rossa.

After a nervy start for St Brigid's, who were playing in their first final, they found their way into the game thanks to Ronan McGrady's scores and they led by two points at half-time.

Despite Diarmuid Rogan's goal for Rossa early in the period, St Brigid's, who were founded in 1998, held on and came out victorious with a two-point win over their cross-city rivals.

O'Donovan Rossa made a great start as Stephen Beatty struck an early two-pointer.

Corey Walsh curled over a brilliant point to make it 0-7 to 0-4 in his side's favour after 15 minutes with St Brigid's struggling to get a foothold in the game.

Sean Fleming's side remained calm under pressure early on, but Brigid's had the antidote.

They came alive following their rocky start, and McGrady was vital, getting the next three scores to draw the sides level after 25 minutes.

JJ Higgins put Cathal Murray's side in the lead for the first time, before Paudie Finnegan and Paul Bradley tagged on further scores to give their side a two-point lead at half-time.

After the break it was more of the same, with Higgins and McGrady doubling up for Brigid's in the first four minutes to increase the lead.

Dominic McEnhill got Rossa going after the break and their urgency paid off when Rogan found himself tapping the game's only goal into an empty net with one point separating the sides early in the second half.

The lead changed hands several times in the half, but St Brigid's remained in control with Higgins getting the final three scores in added time as Rossa looked all at sea.

The final whistle spelt history for St Brigid's as the field filled with blue and yellow flags and flares.

articles.title: Street Fighter Tops the Box Office With $51 Million Opening Weekend Amid Lackluster Reviews
articles.summary: Capcom's Street Fighter movie spun up $51.1 million in its opening weekend, securing its place atop the global box office despite some not-so-great reviews.
articles.body:
Capcom's Street Fighter movie spun up $51.1 million in its opening weekend, securing its place atop the global box office despite some not-so-great reviews.

Ryu (Andrew Koji), Ken (Noah Centineo), and the rest of the film's massive cast grappled with an estimated $31 million domestically and $20.1 million internationally in its theatrical debut. That's a figure that landed it a comfortable first place worldwide, even if it's not a perfect victory across the board.

As audiences turned up for performances – including Callina Liang's Chun-Li, David Dastmalchian's M. Bison, and Jason Momoa's Blanka – not everyone was so happy with how director Kitao Sakurai brought Capcom's classic fighting game franchise to the big screen. In its first few days in the public's gaze, Street Fighter has amassed a critics' score of 44 on IMDb and 41% on Rotten Tomatoes . IGN gave it a 6/10 .

That's serviceable as far as gaming adaptations go and sub-par in the grand scheme. Generally, fans are feeling pretty positive about what they've seen thanks to some crisp animation and fight sequences. " Dumb fun " is one phrase floating around for the film, which doesn't seem to be for everyone but has still pulled in 79% positivity from audiences, according to Rotten Tomatoes.

For comparison (and because Street Fighter actor Andrew Schulz has it on everyone's minds ), the 2021 Mortal Kombat movie earned $22.5 million domestically in its post-lockdown-era debut . Mortal Kombat 2 , which continued that story earlier this year, opened to $63 million globally, coming in second place behind The Devil Wears Prada 2.

That gives Mortal Kombat the edge over its Capcom competitor in terms of direct box office performance worldwide as the teams behind both projects tease ideas for a crossover . The real test for Street Fighter will be its performance in the weeks ahead. Paramount, Legendary, and Capcom made the adaptation with a production budget of $82 million, according to Deadline . We're not quite at that number yet, and if word of those bad reviews spreads too far, the video game movie's fight for a sequel might be more of an uphill battle than expected.

While Street Fighter takes the top box office spot, also in theaters this weekend is Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything . A mind-bending look into the life of controversial Theranos creator Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, the dark-comedy documentary has enraptured moviegoers with $15 million domestically.

That's a number that puts it well below the wide appeal garnered by Street Fighter, but considering the three-hour Fielder doc opened to just 855 theaters compared to the video game movie's 3,575, it's hard not to see You Can See Everything as a more impressive success story. Its production budget reportedly totaled less than $10 million, with its marketing budget also said to be around that same number.

Reviews for the movie are showing incredible positivity, too, with movie reviewer social media platform Letterboxd boasting that You Can See Everything quickly emerged as its highest-rated feature film. IGN's review returned a "Masterpiece" rating of 10/10 . We called it "a jaw-dropping, intimate investigative doc" that "finds TV host Nathan Fielder searching the deep-blue eyes of Silicon Valley scammer Elizabeth Holmes for mysterious answers."

Fielder's latest is only available as a limited release for now. The plan is for it to get a much wider release in the near future, with one Deadline source saying, "Who knows where this will go."

Elsewhere in theaters, moviegoers have had the opportunity to watch two Capcom adaptations as Resident Evil continues its successful run. While star Austin Abrams rides that wave of success, his other picture, Whalefall , which debuted this weekend, only managed to wash up $17.5 million on its $60 million budget.

For more on Street Fighter, you can read why we think it makes a mistake that Mortal Kombat already learned from . You can also see our breakdown of its ending and our list of the best movies of the year .

articles.title: Silent Hill Remake Studio Wants to Make Physical Games 'for as Long as Possible'
articles.summary: Silent Hill developer Bloober Team wants to make physical versions of its games "for as long as possible."
articles.body:
Silent Hill developer Bloober Team wants to make physical versions of its games "for as long as possible."

Studio CEO Piotr Babieno opened up about the company's appreciation for physical media and collectibles during an interview with GamesRadar . He started his thoughts by touching on how the gaming landscape and player desires have changed as technology has advanced over the years, explaining that "we have reached a moment where you can't really do much more" in terms of visual and auditory fidelity.

"Like, OK, the game can have a slightly higher resolution and maybe better lighting and whatever, but will it make it a more engaging game? I don't think so," Babieno said.

The CEO for the studio behind the Silent Hill 2 remake and its in-development original Silent Hill remake also talked about how stats show "the majority of players are playing on hardware which is five, seven years old, if not older." He continued, saying, "But are they less interested in games because of that? I don't think so."

As AI shapes a new, controversial future in the gaming industry, the Bloober executive seems to be more interested in "thinking about other senses." It's this mindset that the team has carried into its new Nintendo Switch 2-exclusive 2.5D horror game, Onyx: The Dark Group . For this experience, which comes from Bloober subsidiary Broken Mirror Games, it's become about "putting horror back in your hands."

"As humans, we have four other senses, and AI can deliver something for what you see, for what you hear, but why not touch?" Babieno said. "I think the physical element of gaming will always, always be there."

When the conversation turned to the topic of physical games – which has become a hot-button issue in the wake of Sony's decision to kill disc releases for PlayStation games , as well as Rockstar's disc-less approach to Grand Theft Auto 6 – Babieno admitted he does see why some are beginning to favor digital releases. After all, as he said, "digital distribution is much easier, much cheaper, and will be more profitable for everyone."

For Babieno, it's hard not to think about how game collecting has affected him, personally, when looking to the future .

"Collecting games also [made] an emotional connection between the game and me, between the studio which produced the game and me," he said. "This little emotional touch is so important that, I think in some way, we would lose the opportunity of being closer with our fans [without it]. So, if we are able to produce a [physical] retail version of our games, we would like to make them for as long as possible."

Also during the interview, Broken Mirror's executive director, Tymon Smektala, who left Dying Light developer Techland to join the Bloober company earlier this year, said that he and Babieno both share a love for game collecting.

"Like, if I could unblur my screen, you would see lots of stuff behind me and I have lots of stuff that's not even in the camera, so this is what gaming is to us," he said during the video interview. "This is the gaming I know, and this is the gaming I expect. And as long as it will be possible, and as long as the big decision makers will allow us to have that, then of course I'll be into that."

Bloober's Silent Hill 2 remake was initially released for PC and PlayStation 5 in 2024 and received physical disc support at the time. Supporting that angle for future games will officially become more complicated when Sony ends support for PlayStation discs in 2028. The Silent Hill 1 remake was announced in June of last year and currently remains without a release date. It's unclear if it will be out before Sony ends support on its end.

articles.title: Antrim SFC: 'Pure relief' as St Brigid's claim first Antrim title
articles.summary: Joseph Finnegan, JJ Higgins and Jack Dowling react to St Brigid's historic first Antrim SFC title after they beat O'Donovan Rossa in the decider.
articles.body:
"Pure relief" was the overriding feeling of many St Brigid's players as the final whistle sounded to confirm their 0-21 to 1-16 win Antrim final over O'Donovan Rossa, which secured their first ever senior football title.

The south Belfast club, founded in 1998, were gracing the Antrim decider for the first time and recovered from a nervy start at Corrigan Park to make history as they finally got their hands on Padraig McNamee Cup.

They fought back from trailing 0-7 to 0-3 at one stage of the first half to lead by two at the break in the all-Belfast decider.

Cathal Murray's side, inspired by teenager JJ Higgins, who kicked seven points, held their nerve in the second half, despite a Rossa goal, to win by two and spark a blue and yellow pitch invasion at full-time.

There were flags, flares and tears of joy as players and fans tried to come to terms with their seismic victory.

"Twenty eight years we've been waiting for this and it's just unreal," club stalwart Joseph Finnegan told BBC Sport NI.

"It's a massive moment for the club. This is only the start for us. It's the best moment of my life bar none."

St Brigid's secure historic first Antrim football title

Higgins turned 19 on Friday and received the perfect belated birthday present in the form of the Padraig McNamee Cup as well as the player of the match award following his sharp shooting display.

"That's what happens when you're younger, you don't have much fear. I kicked a few wides in the first half but I kept going," he said.

"I had a good game against Dunloy (in the semi-final win) and I was still nervous for the final, but sometimes those nerves are good and they get you up for the game."

His teammate Jack Dowling has been togging out for St Brigid's for almost as long as Higgins has been alive, but the 34-year-old praised the teenager's composure on the big stage.

"We did our job and just gave it to the shooters. JJ never does anything spectacular, but he does the simple things repetitively. He's relentless at the simple things."

Dowling's father Dermot was one of St Brigid's founders and Jack is one of the side's most experienced players having been involved in the senior panel for 18 years.

Despite recent setbacks in which getting beyond the semi-final stage was a challenge for the club, he maintained an unwavering belief that they would eventually get to a final and get over the line.

Now, after turning dreams into reality, Dowling said it "didn't seem real" that they have ended the long wait for a maiden title.

"I knew it would come. Someone said to me during the week they didn't think it would ever come, but I knew it would come," he continued.

"I thought it would be sooner than this, but this is sweet."

articles.title: Taika Waititi Says His Star Wars Movie Is 'on Ice'
articles.summary: Director Taika Waititi has confirmed his long-in-development Star Wars movie is officially "on ice."
articles.body:
Director Taika Waititi has confirmed his long-in-development Star Wars movie is officially "on ice."

The Thor: Ragnarok and Jojo Rabbit filmmaker provided Inverse with the update when speaking to the outlet during a press junket for his new film, Klara and the Sun . When asked directly for the state of his and writer Tony McNamara's progress in the Star Wars universe, Waititi had a blunt answer.

"I hate to break this to you, but we're going to actually put it on ice and we're working on a different thing together," he said.

Brutal. Rumors that Disney and Lucasfilm had approached the What We Do in the Shadows filmmaker to helm a Star Wars project go as far back as January 2020. That's just a few years after he took off as the mastermind behind one of the most beloved Marvel Cinematic Universe movies to date, with an official announcement confirming he was attached to a movie arriving just a few months later.

It was mostly good news at first. In 2021, Waititi said he had finished his Star Wars movie's story , and in 2022, then-Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said the goal was to bring it to theaters in late 2023 . At the time, she also admitted that Disney hadn't "locked anything in" quite yet, a fact that only became more apparent in the years that followed.

Waititi was said to be "still working away" on the project on the third anniversary of its announcement in April 2023. After admitting he planned to prioritize other projects later that year, updates went mostly quiet. Waititi finally returned earlier this year to promise that his Star Wars movie was going to "harness a little bit more of the fun from the original trilogy." Now, it's all on ice.

How Much Every Star Wars Movie Made Opening Weekend

"Well, there's your answer," he continued during his conversation with Inverse. "I don't even know how to dress it up or make it even vague. It's very iced. I've got about four other movies I'm trying to do."

It's years of updates that led to what will no doubt arrive as a disappointing announcement for many, even if it's not too surprising. Going on six years with little more than the occasional minor promise never spelled a bright future for Waititi's Star Wars. When Kennedy said she thought the project was "still somewhat alive" amid her Lucasfilm exit , fans started to expect the worst.

None of this is to say Waititi hasn't stayed busy in the years between. In 2022, he launched Thor: Love and Thunder , with his Next Goal Wins movie then following the next year. Klara and the Sun will bring Jenna Ortega, Amy Adams, Steve Buscemi, and the rest of its all-star cast to theaters October 23, 2026, even if negative reviews have cast shade on its premiere. Early reception has landed it with a painful 23% on Rotten Tomatoes after 12 reviews so far.

For now, it's unclear if his Star Wars movie will ever come to be. Even he sounded a bit unsure of what the future holds, adding, "Ice ages do come to an end. Who knows?"

articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg Says He 'Couldn't Get Movie Studio Parts' After Winning His Batman v. Superman Razzie
articles.summary: Jesse Eisenberg says he "couldn't get into studio movie parts" because he won a Worst Supporting Actor Razzie for playing Lex Luthor in Batman v. Superman.
articles.body:
Jesse Eisenberg says he "couldn't get into studio movie parts" because he won a Worst Supporting Actor Razzie for playing Lex Luthor in Batman v. Superman .

The Social Network star elaborated on what has become one of his most divisive roles when speaking at the BFI London Film Festival (via Variety ). He recalled how his time as a long-haired Lex made landing acting roles more challenging, specifically calling attention to how his Golden Raspberry Award win played a part during a difficult time in his career .

"Listen, a lot of it just came from fear," he said when describing his shift away from studio roles. "I couldn’t get into movie studio parts anymore because I had won a Raspberry Award from [being in the] Batman movie … and I saw the trajectory."

Although the polarizing Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice does have its fair share of fans, Eisenberg's more eccentric performance as the Superman villain has remained one of its most controversial elements in the decade since its premiere. His acting was so…memorable that he walked away from the part with a Razzie for Worst Supporting Actor .

Winning at the Golden Raspberry Awards, which recognize the worst components in movies each year, isn't usually treated as an honor. No one wants to be told they are the "worst" at anything, and having that Razzie label attached to your name can sometimes even secure a person's place in the hall of filmmaking infamy.

Eisenberg said that's what his experience was after earning a Razzie for Batman v. Superman, and it's why movie fans didn't see him in as many big films in the years that followed. Instead, he learned to pivot to start writing and directing movies. Two projects to come out of that switch-up are 2024's A Real Pain and The Debut, which will premiere this December.

"If you’re an actor, you’re constantly panicked about 'Am I on an upslope or a downslope?'" he said. "Because there’s no plateau. Acting is just this unstable, awful industry where you are either on the treadmill and you’re doing okay and you’re running up or you are yesterday’s news and it’s awful. And if you’re a paranoid person like me, you see it way in advance."

DCEU Movie Teases That Were Never Paid Off

Eisenberg continued: "The industry tells you what they want from you. The industry did not want me to be in a superhero movie, and if you’re smart and self-aware, you learn that quickly. And you know, it's the unsuccessful actor that goes 'No, I want to be in more of those.' It’s not going to happen and they don't want you there and they wouldn't have given you a Raspberry Award if they wanted you there. That's an award for bad acting. And so the industry tells you what it wants and if you want a career in the arts you have to follow the things that you’re being told are liked."

Although the ex-Lex Luthor actor, who went on to reprise his role in Justice League, has found his footing in the years since his time in the DCEU, Batman v. Superman still has watchers split all these years later. IGN gave the film 6.8/10 review , saying, "BvS is carried by a brutal Batfleck, but as a whole it offers more philosophical drama than superhero escapism."

articles.title: Don Bradman Cricket Jr Announced for PC and Consoles
articles.summary: Don Bradman Cricket Jr Announced for PC and Consoles
articles.body:
With Cricket 26 developer Big Ant Studios holding somewhat of a monopoly on the cricket videogame genre for more than a decade, fans of the world's second most popular sport have been crying out for some competition within the genre. The good news is that Don Bradman Cricket Jr has just been announced by Tru Blu Games. The bad news is that at first glance it seems less like a serious contender confidently striding to the crease, and more like a pitch-invader who's sprinting waywardly around the outfield for a brief bit of fun.

With chunky, cartoon visuals that look like they were created inside Roblox, Don Bradman Cricket Jr appears to be positioning itself as a sort of NBA Jam-esque take on the most beer-friendly of summer sports. The only problem is that Big Ant Studios already had a crack at more or less the same thing way back in 2018 with Big Bash Boom. It featured super-deformed versions of fully licensed BBL and WBBL squads, and packed pyrotechnics into every pull shot and Fortnite-inspired celebration dances for each wicket taken. It was a solid stab at transforming the notoriously complicated sport into a more pick-up-and-play proposition, with our review deeming it to be "a fun, flashy, family-friendly cricket game that’s a bit too light on features to make it a must buy." To date Big Bash Boom remains a one-off experiment, though, with Big Ant opting to focus on the roughly two-yearly cadence of its main simulation-style Cricket series.

In comparison, Don Bradman Cricket Jr is arriving eight years late and minus any official team or player licenses, beyond the inclusion of Australia's greatest ever batsman himself as an unlockable character. By completing a specific in-game challenge, players will apparently be able to drop the Don directly into the otherwise entirely generic Australian team, as well as gain access to a bonus minigame that recreates his famous knocking-a-golf-ball-into-a-water-tank-using-a-stump-fo-a-bat training exercise.

Elsewhere, Don Bradman Cricket Jr seems to be offering a fairly basic feature set, with unlicensed tournaments to play and a challenge mode to test your skills with, alongside split-screen support for two players. Not much is known about the actual gameplay, but the developers are promising that the experience of batting will ensure that "no two shots are ever truly the same." This despite the announcement trailer above seeming to show multiple versions of the same pull through mid-wicket.

Don Bradman Cricket Jr Announcement Screens

Still, this could be a bit of fun for younger cricket fans when it arrives on PC, PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, and Nintendo eShop. No release date has been given for Don Bradman Cricket Jr, however according to Tru Blu Games it's coming soon.

articles.title: The Simpsons’ Apu Has Finally Spoken on the Show for the First Time in Almost a Decade
articles.summary: The Simpsons’ Apu Has Finally Spoken on the Show for the First Time in Almost a Decade
articles.body:
After some nine years of being seen but not heard on The Simpsons, the show's creators have finally given a voice back to beloved Kwik-E-Mart owner, Apu Nahasapeemapetilon. In episode three of the series' 38th season dubbed "The Revengening", which aired Sunday night on Fox in the US, a new voice for the loveable Squishee salesman was debuted courtesy of actor and voice-over veteran, Sunil Malhotra (Grey's Anatomy, The Legend of Korra).

According to a report on Variety , Malhotra's hiring and the return of the Apu character – who hasn't uttered a single word on the show since the October 2017 episode, "The Serfsons" – have been heavily kept under wraps, with producers keeping both the episode's table read and its subsequent production under strict NDA for everyone involved.

"We love this character, and wanted to bring him back in a smart, Simpsons-y way that allowed him to evolve," executive producer Matt Selman told Variety. "We're excited by what Sunil has already brought to the role, and look forward to seeing more of Apu in the future."

The Simpsons: Every Treehouse of Horror Episode Ranked

Hank Azaria previously voiced Apu for the first 29 seasons of the animated series. However, after the character became the focus of the 2017 documentary "The Problem With Apu", in which comedian Hari Kondabolu discussed the negative impact the character has had on people of South Asian descent, Azaria announced that he would no longer lend his voice to the role . Later, during an episode of Dax Shepard's Armchair Expert in 2021, Azaria reflected with remorse about his portrayal of the character and stated that part of him "feels like I need to go to every single Indian person in this country and personally apologise."

After Azaria vacated the role, Apu was pushed to the background on The Simpsons, occasionally seen but never heard. However, after an idea to bring the character back for one of season 38's Halloween-themed episodes was hatched by staffer Nick Hahan and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos, the process of finding a new actor for Apu began in earnest.

“When my agent called me about a ‘Simpsons’ audition, I knew exactly what role it was for, and the idea actually made my stomach sink,” Malhotra told Variety. “But admittedly, part of me was also curious. It had been eight years since Apu had spoken on the show, and it got me thinking: Did the writers’ room look different now? Could they bring him back in a way that acknowledged and apologized for past mistakes? Could I make the character my own, and reclaim him in some way? And could they achieve all of that in an unmistakably ‘Simpsons’ way that didn’t disappoint fans?"

We Build LEGO The Simpsons: Krusty Burger

After some back and forth with the show's producers, Malhotra was eventually convinced that the return of Apu was being handled in the best possible way.

"It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for longtime fans of ‘The Simpsons’ and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way," said Malhotra.

In "The Revengening", a man in a Daft Punk-inspired Halloween costume is accidentally killed over and over again by residents of Springfield. A year later, the man is still alive and taking his revenge on his would-be killers, one at a time. Eventually the costumed killer is unmasked and revealed to be Apu, who tells the town's residents, "I am the man you left for dead. I am the one you pretended never existed!"

To which Marge, seemingly serving as a mouthpiece for the show's producers, replies, "Apu, we're so sorry we left you for dead. Believe me, wanted to do the right thing." Bart then adds, "But we were so scared, and just didn't know what to do."

For his part, Malhotra seems satisfied with Apu's reintroduction to the cast.

“I’d be lying if I didn’t say that the sweetest part of all was unleashing that righteously rage-fueled “I AM APU!” — on behalf of so many of us — over and over in the studio until we got it just right,” said Malhotra. “I really feel like we did and I can’t wait for fans to see more Apu.”

Have you watched "The Revengening"? What do you think of Sunil Malhotra's portrayal of Apu? Is it a thank you, come again? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Rays Take Control of ALCS With Gritty Game 5 Victory Over Guardians
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Moves One Win Away From the World Series The Tampa Bay Rays are one win away from reaching the World Series after defeating the Cleveland Guardians...
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Moves One Win Away From the World Series

The Tampa Bay Rays are one win away from reaching the World Series after defeating the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 in Game 5 of the American League Championship Series on Sunday. Behind another outstanding postseason performance from starting pitcher Drew Rasmussen and timely hitting throughout the lineup, Tampa Bay took a 3-2 lead in the best of seven series.

The Rays entered the matchup looking to build on Saturday's 7-3 victory, which evened the series at two games apiece. They delivered another strong performance in Cleveland, putting themselves in position to clinch the American League pennant on their home field.

Drew Rasmussen Delivers Another Strong Start

Rasmussen was the biggest difference-maker Sunday, holding Cleveland to one run on four hits across seven innings. He consistently kept the Guardians' hitters off balance, limiting scoring opportunities and giving Tampa Bay's offense time to build an advantage.

The outing continued Rasmussen's impressive postseason run. His performance helped the Rays control the game from the early innings and put pressure on Cleveland to find answers against Tampa Bay's pitching staff.

Rasmussen's ability to work deep into the game also protected the bullpen, allowing the Rays to turn the final two innings over to their relievers with a lead.

Bryan Baker eventually closed out the victory, recording his fifth save of the postseason as Tampa Bay held off Cleveland's late push.

Rays Get Timely Contributions at the Plate

Tampa Bay established control early, building a 3-0 advantage through the first three innings. Jonny DeLuca drove in the opening run, Jonathan Aranda added an RBI single, and Liam Hicks delivered another run scoring hit.

Yandy Díaz also played an important role, collecting three hits and scoring a run. His consistent production at the plate helped Tampa Bay generate offense without relying on a home run.

Cleveland managed to get on the scoreboard in the sixth inning when Chase DeLauter drove in a run. However, the Guardians could not produce the additional offense needed to erase the deficit.

The victory gives Tampa Bay a chance to finish the series at Tropicana Field. Game 6 is scheduled for Monday, with the Rays needing just one more win to advance.

For Cleveland, the pressure is now significant. The Guardians must win to extend their season and force a decisive Game 7.

Tampa Bay has momentum, strong starting pitching and an opportunity to clinch at home. After winning two straight games in Cleveland, the Rays are closing in on a return to the World Series.

articles.title: Rays on the verge of ensuring ultra-rare World Series phenomenon
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays are being pushed to their limit by the Cleveland Guardians. Nonetheless, over the past two days, the Rays have shown why they were the bes...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays are being pushed to their limit by the Cleveland Guardians. Nonetheless, over the past two days, the Rays have shown why they were the best team in the AL this past season. After falling down 2-1 in the ALCS, the Rays have bounced back with two consecutive victories on the road — with Tampa Bay having taken a 3-2 lead in the series courtesy of a 3-1 win on Sunday.

With that victory, the Rays are now knocking on the door of the World Series, where the Milwaukee Brewers await. It seems like the postponement of Friday night's contest due to inclement weather helped them immensely, as Game 6 (as well as Game 7, if necessary) will be at Tropicana Field — giving Tampa Bay a golden opportunity to secure their third appearance in the Fall Classic.

Moreover, if the Rays were to win another game against the Guardians in the ALCS, they would ensure a rare World Series phenomenon with the Milwaukee Brewers already waiting on the other side of the bracket. As per Rays insider Steve Carney, if Tampa Bay were to advance to the next round, this would be the first World Series matchup in 46 years between two teams that have never won a title.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

In 1980, the Kansas City Royals and Philadelphia Phillies faced off against each other for a chance to win their first World Series title. In the end, it was the Phillies that got the better of the Royals, winning the series 4-2. The Royals would get their breakthrough in 1985 and would follow that up with another title in 2015.

The Brewers, like the Rays, have been in the World Series before. However, Milwaukee has only had just one shot at winning a title, and they whiffed it back in 1982 — losing in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals.

Meanwhile, the Rays have made it to the Fall Classic twice, falling to the Phillies and the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2008 and 2020, respectively. Can they make it three World Series appearances for the franchise with a win either on Monday night or on Tuesday (if necessary)?
